payload.prompt: What is tokenization?

options.text: Breaking text into tokens and assigning IDs
options.rationale: Tokenization separates text into distinct tokens and assigns identifiers. This prepares language for model processing.
Embeddings are contextual representations created after token preparation. They do not split text into tokens.
options.better_fit: Use this for encoder processing that creates contextual representations.

options.rationale: Position information identifies where an occurrence appears. It does not determine the token pieces.
options.better_fit: Use this when sequence order must be represented.

options.rationale: Next-token prediction generates a likely continuation. Tokenization prepares the input first.
options.better_fit: Use this for decoder output generation.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Tokenization prepares text as identifiable tokens.

payload.prompt: Which can be tokens? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: A whole word can be a vocabulary token. Tokens are not restricted to whole words.
A reusable sub-word can be a token. It can represent part of a longer word.
Punctuation can be tokenized. Vocabularies can contain common character sequences.
A position describes where a token occurs. It is not a token in the vocabulary.
options.better_fit: Use positional encoding to represent occurrence order.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Tokens can be words, sub-words, punctuation, or other common character sequences.

payload.prompt: Is the following statement accurate?
payload.statement: Tokenization breaks text only into complete words, never sub-words or punctuation.
payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Tokens can include sub-words and punctuation.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: That choice would exclude valid token types.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Tokenization may use words, sub-words, punctuation, and other common character sequences.

payload.prompt: Complete the statement with the technical term.

parts.text: In the word "unlikely," the piece "un" can be a

payload.explanation: Tokenization can break language into sub-word pieces, not only complete words.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The answer would not name the kind of token represented by "un."
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: A sub-word is a token that represents part of a word.

payload.prompt: A developer must split an incoming sentence into words, punctuation, and common character pieces before the model processes it. Which method should the developer choose?

options.rationale: Tokenization splits language into usable tokens. It is the required preparation step.
Positional encoding records where tokens occur. It does not create the token pieces.
options.better_fit: Use this after tokens are identified to represent sequence order.

feedback.intrinsic: The developer would have locations without first defining the pieces.
feedback.instructional: Choose tokenization to split the text; use positional encoding for order.

options.rationale: Embeddings are created from token representations in context. They do not perform the initial split.
options.better_fit: Use this when an encoder creates contextual vectors.

feedback.intrinsic: Processing would start before the input was divided into tokens.

options.error_type: Confuses input preparation with output generation
options.rationale: Prediction chooses a likely continuation. It does not prepare the supplied sentence.
options.better_fit: Use this when generating a response token.

feedback.intrinsic: The workflow would jump to generation too early.
feedback.instructional: Prepare input with tokenization before predicting output.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Tokenization produces the token pieces needed for later processing.

payload.prompt: Which statements about token IDs are correct? Select all that apply.

options.text: A token ID is an integer
options.rationale: A token ID is a unique integer. It identifies a vocabulary token.

options.text: Each distinct vocabulary token has an ID
options.rationale: Vocabulary entries receive identifiers. These IDs distinguish distinct tokens.

options.text: A repeated token keeps its ID
options.rationale: The ID belongs to the vocabulary token. Repeating that token does not create a new ID.
An ID identifies which token appears. Position identifies where an occurrence appears.
options.better_fit: Use positional encoding to show sequence location.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. IDs identify vocabulary tokens rather than their locations.

payload.prompt: In a vocabulary, what does a token ID identify?

options.rationale: An ID is assigned to a distinct vocabulary token. Each occurrence of that token uses the same ID.
A token can appear at multiple positions. Its ID remains associated with its vocabulary identity.
options.better_fit: Use positional encoding for a token occurrence's location.

options.rationale: A dimension is one value inside a vector. A token ID identifies a vocabulary entry.
options.better_fit: Use this for an individual numeric value in a vector.

options.rationale: A decoder prediction selects a likely token. An ID labels tokens available in the vocabulary.
options.better_fit: Use this for the likely next token selected by a decoder.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. A token ID identifies one distinct vocabulary token.

payload.prompt: Evaluate this statement.
payload.statement: If "a" appears twice, both occurrences use the same token ID.
payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Repeating a vocabulary token does not create another ID.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: A repeated token would incorrectly become a new vocabulary entry.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: IDs identify token identity, while positional encoding distinguishes occurrences.

payload.prompt: Arrange the parts to form a correct statement.
payload.explanation: A token's identifier is reused whenever that vocabulary token appears.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The rule for repeated vocabulary items would be unclear.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: State the repeated token first, then that it retains its assigned ID.

payload.prompt: What is a vector in this context?

options.rationale: A vector contains multiple numeric values. Its individual values are dimensions.
A token ID is one integer. A vector is an array containing multiple values.
options.better_fit: Use this to identify a distinct vocabulary token.

options.rationale: Location in a sequence is positional information. A vector is a numeric representation.
options.better_fit: Use this when recording where a token occurs.

options.rationale: A predicted token is a generation result. A vector represents information used in processing.
options.better_fit: Use this when describing a decoder's selected continuation.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. A vector is an array with multiple numeric dimensions.

payload.prompt: Which statements describe a token vector? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: This is an array of numeric values. That is the form of a vector.
Each individual numeric value in a vector is a dimension. Vectors contain multiple dimensions.
Token vectors encode language and meaning attributes. They can also represent relationships to other tokens.

options.text: It is a unique integer ID
options.rationale: A unique integer identifies a token. A vector is a multi-value numeric array.
options.better_fit: Use this when naming a vocabulary token with its ID.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Token vectors are numeric arrays that encode token attributes.

payload.prompt: True or false?
payload.statement: A token vector is a single unique integer used to identify a token.
payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. That describes a token ID, not a vector.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The token's representation would be mistaken for its identifier.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: A vector contains multiple numeric values; a token ID is one integer.

payload.prompt: Complete the sentence with the correct term.

parts.text: The individual numeric values in a vector are called

payload.explanation: A vector is made of numeric elements, each called a dimension.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The chosen term would not name one numeric element of a vector.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Token IDs identify tokens and embeddings are contextual vectors; individual values are dimensions.

payload.prompt: Order the pieces to form a correct statement.
payload.explanation: Beyond representing language and meaning attributes, token vectors encode how a token relates to other tokens.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The statement would no longer express what token vectors can encode.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Begin with token vectors, then state that they encode relationships between tokens.

payload.prompt: A developer represents the token "heard" as [2, 15, 1] to encode language and meaning attributes. What should the developer call this representation?

options.rationale: The representation is an array of numeric values. Such an array can encode token attributes.
A token ID is one integer for a vocabulary entry. The displayed representation has several numeric values.
options.better_fit: Use this for the single integer assigned to "heard" in the vocabulary.

feedback.intrinsic: The array's dimensions would be reduced to one identifier.
feedback.instructional: An array such as [2, 15, 1] is a token vector, not a token ID.

options.rationale: Positional encoding represents sequence location. The array in this scenario represents token attributes.
options.better_fit: Use this to indicate where "heard" occurs in the sentence.

feedback.intrinsic: The token's representation would be confused with its location.
feedback.instructional: Position shows order; a token vector encodes attributes.

options.rationale: A completion is generated language. A numeric array is a representation used by the model.
options.better_fit: Use this for text produced after next-token prediction.

feedback.intrinsic: Numeric data would incorrectly be treated as generated language.
feedback.instructional: Vectors represent tokens; completions are generated sequences.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. The numeric array is a token vector.

payload.prompt: Which statements about initial vectors and position are correct? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Initial vectors are randomly assigned before becoming embeddings. They are later transformed through processing.

options.text: Position tells where a token occurs
options.rationale: Positional encoding supplies a token occurrence's location. This provides order information.
Changing order changes how tokens relate. Positional encoding helps preserve that distinction.

options.text: Each occurrence needs a new token ID
options.rationale: Repeated tokens retain their vocabulary ID. Different positions distinguish their occurrences.
options.better_fit: Use a new ID for a genuinely distinct vocabulary token.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Initial vectors begin randomly and position preserves meaningful order.

payload.prompt: Decide whether this statement is true or false.
payload.statement: The same token can keep one token ID while appearing at different positions.
payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Token identity and sequence location are separate.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: A repeated token would be treated as new simply because it appeared later.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: The ID identifies the token; positional encoding shows its occurrence location.

payload.prompt: Reconstruct the preparation sequence.
payload.explanation: Initial representations are assigned, order information is added, and the prepared representations are sent to the transformer.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The preparation sequence would be out of order.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Assign vectors first, add position information, then send the prepared tokens onward.

payload.prompt: Complete the sentence with the correct term.

parts.text: Information that tells the model where a token occurs in a sequence is

payload.explanation: Positional encoding represents sequence location, which matters because order changes token relationships.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The selected term would not communicate sequence location.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Token IDs identify tokens, while positional encoding records where occurrences appear.

payload.prompt: A developer prepares a sentence containing two occurrences of "a" and must preserve their different locations. Which choices should the developer make? Select all that apply.

options.text: Reuse the same token ID for both
options.rationale: Both occurrences are the same vocabulary token. They therefore use the same assigned ID.

options.text: Give each occurrence a different position
options.rationale: The occurrences appear at different places in the sequence. Their positional information must differ.

options.text: Apply positional encoding to each occurrence
options.rationale: Each occurrence needs order information. Positional encoding provides this information.

options.text: Create a new vocabulary token for the second occurrence
options.error_type: Confuses repetition with a new token
options.rationale: A repeated occurrence is not a distinct vocabulary entry. It should reuse the known token ID.
options.better_fit: Use this only when the vocabulary gains a genuinely distinct token.

feedback.intrinsic: The vocabulary would grow without a new token being introduced.
feedback.instructional: Reuse the ID and use different positional encodings for the occurrences.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Identity stays the same while positional information changes.

payload.prompt: What does a transformer model do?

options.text: Transforms representations and predicts next tokens
options.rationale: A transformer creates embeddings from token representations and predicts probable next tokens. Its architecture includes encoder and decoder components.
Assigning IDs occurs during tokenization. A transformer performs representation and prediction work.
options.better_fit: Use this while preparing vocabulary tokens.

options.rationale: Position information indicates order. A transformer uses representations to create embeddings and make predictions.
options.better_fit: Use this when supplying sequence-location information.

options.rationale: Instructions can establish response behavior or tone. They are not the transformer architecture.
options.better_fit: Use this for a system instruction that guides style.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. A transformer creates contextual representations and predicts likely next tokens.

payload.prompt: Which are parts or capabilities of a transformer? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: A transformer includes an encoder block. The encoder helps create embeddings.
A transformer includes a decoder layer. The decoder predicts probable next tokens.
Transformers transform token representations into embeddings. This is part of their processing role.
Response tone is set by instructions. It is not a transformer component or capability.
options.better_fit: Use this for instructions that guide response style.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Transformers include encoder and decoder components and create embeddings.

payload.prompt: Is the following statement accurate?
payload.statement: A transformer has only an encoder block and no decoder layer.
payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. A transformer includes both an encoder block and a decoder layer.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The architecture's prediction component would be omitted.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: The encoder creates embeddings, while the decoder predicts probable next tokens.

payload.prompt: Complete the sentence with the correct term.

parts.text: The model architecture with an encoder block and decoder layer is a

payload.explanation: A transformer contains encoder and decoder components and processes token representations.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The answer would name a component or representation rather than the architecture.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: The full architecture containing encoder and decoder parts is a transformer.

payload.prompt: A developer needs an architecture that turns token representations into contextual embeddings and then chooses the most probable next token. Which architecture should the developer choose?

options.rationale: A transformer creates embeddings and predicts likely next tokens. Its encoder and decoder support these tasks.
Tokenization splits text and assigns IDs. It does not create contextual embeddings or predict continuations.
options.better_fit: Use this to prepare the input before model processing.

feedback.intrinsic: The text would be prepared but no prediction architecture would be selected.
feedback.instructional: Tokenization prepares tokens; a transformer creates embeddings and predicts tokens.

options.rationale: Positional encoding supplies location information. It is not an encoder-decoder architecture.
options.better_fit: Use this alongside token representations when order matters.

feedback.intrinsic: Order would be available but the stated processing system would be absent.
feedback.instructional: Position conveys order; a transformer performs embedding and prediction work.

options.rationale: A system prompt guides behavior and constraints. It does not transform vectors or make next-token predictions.
options.better_fit: Use this to specify response behavior or tone.

feedback.intrinsic: Instructions alone would not provide the requested model computation.
feedback.instructional: Prompts guide behavior; transformer architecture processes and predicts tokens.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. A transformer supplies both contextual representation and next-token prediction.

payload.prompt: Which statements correctly match transformer blocks to their work? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: The encoder creates contextual embeddings. It applies attention to token vectors.
The decoder uses embeddings to predict the next probable token. This supports sequential generation.
Attention is applied in the encoder. It helps produce a strong vector representation.
Token IDs are assigned during tokenization. The decoder uses representations and prediction components instead.
options.better_fit: Use this while creating identifiers for vocabulary tokens.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. The encoder creates embeddings and the decoder predicts probable tokens.

payload.prompt: Evaluate this statement.
payload.statement: The decoder uses embeddings, attention, and a feed-forward neural network to predict the next most probable token.
payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Those components support the decoder's next-token prediction.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The prediction process would omit components used to choose a continuation.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: The decoder uses embeddings, attention, and a feed-forward neural network to predict a likely next token.

payload.prompt: Put the processing steps in order.
payload.explanation: Embeddings are created before the decoder uses them, and that use supports next-token prediction.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: Prediction would incorrectly precede the representations it requires.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Place encoder work first, then decoder use of embeddings, then prediction.

payload.prompt: Complete the sentence with the correct term.

parts.text: The transformer block that creates embeddings is the

payload.explanation: The encoder applies attention and a fully connected neural network to create embeddings.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The answer would name the prediction block or a different component.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: The encoder creates embeddings; the decoder predicts the next token.

payload.prompt: A developer already has embeddings for a prompt and must predict its next most probable token. Which decoder capabilities should the developer use? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: The decoder uses encoder-created embeddings. They provide contextual representations for prediction.
The decoder uses attention while predicting. Attention helps it consider relevant sequence context.
The decoder uses a feed-forward neural network. It contributes to choosing a probable candidate.

options.text: New token IDs for each word
options.rationale: Token IDs are assigned during tokenization. The decoder predicts using embeddings, attention, and a feed-forward network.
options.better_fit: Use this only when assigning IDs to distinct vocabulary tokens.

feedback.intrinsic: Vocabulary identities would be changed instead of using prediction components.
feedback.instructional: For prediction, use embeddings, attention, and a feed-forward neural network; do not assign new IDs.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. The decoder uses embeddings, attention, and a feed-forward neural network to predict the next token.

flashcards.back: It breaks text into tokens and assigns each token an ID.
A unique integer that identifies a token in the vocabulary.
Information that tells the model where a token appears in a sequence.
It creates embeddings from token vectors using attention.
